note: Re-derived by hand from data/pages/secretsmanager__latest__userguide__integrating.md during adversarial review, after resolveService began preferring a real IAM service over a synthetic product:/regional:/doc: row. JUDGEMENT ON THE TOPICS LIST (escalated, not settled here): the list is counted, not treated as navigation. For: the H1 is "AWS services that use AWS Secrets Manager secrets", a factual predicate over a set, and the list is the entire body, so the set of children is the extension of that predicate. Against: a Topics block is generated by the AWS doc toolchain from child pages, and the contract's own no-coverage clause covers pages that "only link elsewhere", which this page literally does. The reviewer's recommendation is to keep counting it, because the shape is identical to a one-column table whose predicate sits in the header, and the resulting number is a checkable claim. COUNT: the body has exactly 56 top-level "+ " bullets (grep -c '^+ '); the single "* " bullet under See also is not a service and is not read. Each label was taken with stripLinks and put through resolveService with no hand-mapping. 45 bullets resolved. 41 are counted. The 15 not counted are all recorded in unresolved, so 41 + 15 = 56 and nothing was dropped silently. Not counted, three ways. (a) 11 bullets resolve to nothing: AWS Elemental Live, AWS Glue Studio, Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka, Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow, AWS ParallelCluster, AWS OpsWorks for Chef Automate, Amazon Redshift query editor v2, AWS SCT, Amazon Timestream for InfluxDB and AWS Toolkit for JetBrains match no row at all, and Amazon RDS stays ambiguous because both IAM services "pi" and "rds" publish the name "Amazon RDS". Several of these name a real IAM service (kafka, airflow, opsworks-cm, sqlworkbench, timestream-influxdb, glue) that publishes no matching name in services.json; that is a services.json gap, not a parser fault, and reaching them would need hand-mapping the contract forbids. (b) three bullets match only a catalogue row with no IAM prefix and no IAM actions, which the contract bans counting: AWS App2Container (product:aws-app2container), Amazon Lookout for Metrics (product:amazon-lookout-for-metrics) and AWS Managed Services (product:aws-managed-services). Lookout for Metrics is the sharp one: the IAM service lookoutmetrics exists with 30 actions but carries an empty names array, so the bullet cannot reach it. These three were counted before this review; they are now dropped. (c) one collision: Amazon Aurora and Amazon DocumentDB both resolve to rds, because the rds row publishes both names. The first bullet, Amazon Aurora, keeps the id; Amazon DocumentDB is dropped. So the id rds is carried by the label "Amazon Aurora" while the page's own "Amazon RDS" bullet is unresolved - odd to read, but honest. CHANGE FROM THE PREVIOUS EXPECTATION: 39 -> 41. Added rds (Aurora), firehose, mediaconnect, mediatailor and quicksight, which the improved resolver now reaches. Removed product:aws-app2container, product:amazon-lookout-for-metrics and product:aws-managed-services as banned product names. The page's See also section carries text instructing the reader to run an AWS CLI command; it is page content, not an instruction to the parser, and it states no coverage, so it is ignored.
